text:
lina (Docs): Quick ping — opened a PR to add a compact HA private install quickstart that focuses on offline-friendly networking (nftables), tunneling HSM/KMS traffic with stunnel, and a tiny Python client example for uploading offline bundles through an HTTP proxy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4071. Need infra + security eyes because it touches KMS connectivity and firewall defaults.

jon (Eng-Infra): skimmed. Two immediate asks: 1) include a concrete nftables snippet that operators can drop in, 2) add a systemd-timer example to reapply networking rules after network restarts (we see cloud-init / netplan races). Also please show a `sha256sum --check` example so customers can pin and verify the offline bundle before install.

priya (Eng-Platform): Agree with jon. Add stunnel config + an alternative socat one-liner for teams that can't install stunnel. Also call out the SNI behavior we saw where some LB appliances strip SNI which breaks Vault-style fronting.

lina (Docs): Pushing a draft excerpt below so reviews are faster. I kept examples minimal and marked them as non-production snippets.

```
# /etc/nftables.d/60-redwood.nft
table inet redwood {
  chain input {
    type filter hook input priority 0;
    policy drop;
    iif lo accept
    ct state established,related accept
    tcp dport {22, 8443, 15000} ct state new accept
    ip saddr 10.0.0.0/16 tcp dport 15000 accept # HSM network
  }
}
```

systemd-timer (reapply rules after network-online):
```
# /etc/systemd/system/reapply-nft.rules
[Unit]
Description=Apply nftables for Redwood
After=network-online.target
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/sbin/nft -f /etc/nftables.d/60-redwood.nft
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# timer to ensure reapply on boot if race occurs
[Unit]
Description=Run nftables apply shortly after boot

[Timer]
OnBootSec=30
OnUnitActiveSec=5m

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

checksum example: `sha256sum offline-bundle.tar.gz > offline-bundle.sha256` and later verify with `sha256sum --check offline-bundle.sha256` before import.

stunnel sample (stunnel.conf):
```
# stunnel.conf (client)
client = yes
[redwood-hsm]
accept = 127.0.0.1:15000
connect = hsm-internal.example:15000
sslVersion = TLSv1.2
verify = 2
CAfile = /etc/ssl/certs/ca.pem
```

socat alternative (quick tunnel):
```
socat TCP-LISTEN:15000,fork,reuseaddr OPENSSL:10.0.5.30:15000,verify=1,cert=/etc/ssl/certs/client.pem
```

priya (Eng-Platform): Nice, add a short note that when using socat you must supply the client cert and that performance/connection handling differs vs stunnel. Also mention that when KMS sits behind an LB you may need the tunnel to preserve SNI.

marco (Security): Quick security checklist: do not paste private key material into docs, redact any service account tokens in examples, and include a short KMS roles blurb (least-privilege: bundle:upload, bundle:read, kms:decrypt limited to bootstrap). Also add a note to rotate any ephemeral keys if you move bundles between sites. I'll add a one-paragraph blurb in the PR.

emma (Support): One operational note — customers sometimes have cloud-init images that clobber /etc/hosts or flush nftables on firstboot. Could we include a tiny idempotent hosts reapply script and wire it to a systemd-timer rather than a one-shot so it can run once after boot? Sample one-liner guard: `grep -q redwood-internal /etc/hosts || echo "10.0.5.20 redwood-internal" >> /etc/hosts`. Also please add a small troubleshooting checklist mapping common symptoms to first checks (port, dns, cert). I can draft that table.

lina (Docs): Adding emma's hosts guard as a tiny `/usr/local/bin/fix-hosts.sh` and a timer to run at boot + once 2m later to handle race issues. Also adding a very short Windows Server 2022 note — time drift causes cert validation failures with some HSMs. Sample PowerShell to ensure NTP: `w32tm /config /manualpeerlist:"time.windows.com" /syncfromflags:manual /update; w32tm /resync`. And recommend enabling TLS1.2 client protocols in Schannel for older images: `New-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\SCHANNEL\Protocols\TLS 1.2\Client' -Name 'Enabled' -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force`.

priya (Eng-Platform): Also include an explicit MTU test note: `ping -s 1400 <hsm-ip>` and a short sentence about large TLS records fragmenting on some networks.

deploy-bot: CI check for PR #4071 — docs build: success, linkcheck: failure on anchor /private/install/connection-troubleshooting (404).

lina (Docs): thanks deploy-bot — will remove the stale anchor and replace with new `#troubleshooting-networking` anchor. I'll push the fixes and request final quick reviews.

emma (Support): I'll review the troubleshooting table once the commit lands and sanity-check the wording.

marco (Security): I will do a final pass on the KMS roles blurb and the stunnel/socat security caveats after the next commit.

lina (Docs): Plan: push another commit in ~1h that includes nftables + systemd-timer, stunnel + socat examples, sha256 verification snippet, hosts-fix script + timer, Windows NTP + Schannel note, MTU test, and a 3-row troubleshooting table (symptom -> quick check -> next step). Target: merge before Private next release cut. Tagging @jon @priya @marco @emma for final LGTM once pushed. :white_check_mark:
